remaining_material_problem: Reliable cross-system exception evidence remains incomplete: cross-channel, transfer, return, inventory, and accounting questions still depend on source evidence and platform maturity.
confidence_qualifier: Confident for the deterministic synthetic fixtures; not validated with a real customer.

rationales.technical: Identity, native configuration, integrations, automation, BI, and process rules removed routine work, but did not create missing accounting evidence or uniformly close cross-system gaps.
rationales.business_question_coverage: Coverage improved materially, while several questions remained partial, unanswered, or source-limited.
rationales.residual_burden: Chapter 11 retains broad operational and administrative burdens; Chapter 17 isolates one useful bounded portion rather than all residuals.
rationales.support: Chapter 12's configuration surface is manageable but recurring, and automation failures still require support.
rationales.scaling: Store #7 reused standardized structure without a new code path.
rationales.fragmentation: Store #8 sharply reduced reuse and made standardization or migration a prerequisite to durable integration.
rationales.economics: Chapter 19 makes BUY / CONFIGURE the first-year leader and full custom the three-year leader; no single option wins both horizons.
rationales.sensitivity: The modeled sensitivity set leaves full custom as the three-year leader, but horizon disagreement makes the result TOO_CLOSE rather than robust.
rationales.decision: Mixed capability, broad residuals, high platform dependence, and split economic leaders prevent a responsible BUY / CONFIGURE, narrow-edge, or full-custom commitment before discovery.
